plain_english_revision: This amendment by Rep. Daniels replaces the entire Special Order Calendar with a prioritized list of bills that would be debated and voted on during the next legislative day (the 22nd). The amendment does not change the underlying bill's purpose but instead dictates which specific bills take precedence over all other business for one session day.
candidate_position_supported: Advancing a targeted legislative agenda by prioritizing select bills on the Special Order Calendar to expedite their consideration during a single legislative day.
evidence_quotes: BE IT RESOLVED BY THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES... that immediately upon adoption of this resolution, the following business... shall be the special and paramount order of business for the 22nd legislative day taking precedence over the regular order of business or any pending or unfinished business.
HB597: Law enforcement officers, murdered in line of duty, state employee granted administrative leave for trial under certain conditions
HB379: Crimes and offenses, sex offenses, mandatory condition of parole, chemical castration treatment authorized as mandatory condition of parole for certain sex offenders
review_reason: The amendment is procedural in nature but clearly outlines specific bills that would be prioritized. The direction and valence are indeterminate because the amendment does not explicitly state an ideological stance, only a procedural change.
